def: An insurer pays an agreed benefit when a specified heat index crosses the policy threshold, without assessing each person's actual income loss.
pays: Member, employer or sponsor; identify separately by policy year.
gets: Insured person or a named beneficiary through the contracted channel.
speed: Index calculation avoids individual loss adjustment; days-to-cash is not verified for the example.
good: Can insure income disruption without damaged property.
limits: Thresholds, caps and bank access can leave serious needs unfunded.
basis: Location, metric and threshold may miss individual harm; payout can also exceed personal loss.

n: Parametric heat insurance - employers and organisations
def: A business or intermediary buys heat-triggered cover for its own costs or a specified group.
gets: Organisation or covered workers; these are different arrangements.
speed: Potentially fast after index confirmation; published launch is not proof of payment speed.
good: Aggregates buyers and may simplify enrolment.
limits: Employer receipt alone does not prove worker benefit; limited benefit can be mistaken for full wage replacement.
basis: Regional weather data may miss worksite exposure.

def: A government transfers a defined heat-related fiscal risk using an agreed index.
gets: Treasury or designated public agency, then services or households.
speed: Design-dependent; no verified sovereign heat payout benchmark in this review.
good: Could fund health or income response without asset destruction.
limits: No issued sovereign heat policy was verified here; do not present the category as an operating scheme.
basis: Fiscal spending and population harm may not track one temperature index.

def: Pays eligible, evidenced business losses under the actual policy wording; heat is covered only if its cause and loss meet that wording.
speed: After evidence and adjustment; no heat-specific observed timing verified.
good: Can reflect actual insured financial loss.
limits: Ordinary business interruption may require insured physical damage; heat alone would ideally not be assumed covered.
basis: Coverage and loss-definition mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk.

def: Compensates eligible yield shortfall under notified crop and area rules. An area-yield contract uses average area yield, not each farm's loss.
pays: Farmer plus public subsidy where applicable.
speed: Dependent on crop-cutting/yield data and settlement; seasonal timing may miss immediate heat needs.
good: Connects finance to production loss.
limits: PMFBY is included as a direct yield-loss design model; specific heat eligibility is not verified by the source's named-peril list.
basis: Area-yield averages can miss a particular farm's loss; heat cause may be disputed.

def: Reimburses the eligible insured loss of livestock, after veterinary and policy checks.
speed: Requires loss evidence; no heat-specific settlement benchmark verified.
good: Can match an eligible animal loss.
limits: Heat death, reduced milk yield and disease are distinct coverages; no primary heat indemnity wording verified here.
basis: No index basis risk in individual loss adjustment; substantial coverage and valuation risk.

n: Health expense indemnity and employment-injury protection
def: Health indemnity reimburses eligible expenses; employment-injury systems provide specified medical or earnings benefits where heat illness qualifies.
pays: Household, employer, social contributions or public funds.
gets: Patient, provider or eligible worker, depending on benefit.
speed: Cashless care and reimbursement have different timing; no generic heat benchmark.
good: Responds to diagnosed illness rather than an outdoor temperature alone.
limits: Not all health-related insurance is indemnity: the Japanese example is a fixed clinical-event benefit.
basis: No weather-index mismatch; diagnosis, access and eligibility can still exclude heat harm.

n: Fixed benefit for a heat-related clinical event
def: Pays a set amount for a covered medical event such as qualifying heatstroke treatment; it is neither weather-parametric nor expense indemnity.
speed: After clinical documentation; observed settlement time not verified.
good: Concrete heat-specific health trigger.
limits: Cannot finance prevention before illness; clinical access shapes who can claim.
basis: No weather basis risk; harm without the specified clinical event can go unpaid.

def: Countries use shared insurance infrastructure and risk capital, often with reinsurance, to finance agreed disaster losses.
gets: Insured government; people receive funds only through a further delivery step.
speed: Lao PDR verified sovereign receipt benchmark is in its scheme record; it is not household timing.
good: Shares capacity, infrastructure and contingency planning.
limits: Diversification may weaken for correlated regional heat; no pool heat payout verified here.
basis: Index/impact reporting may miss losses and uncounted people.

def: Investors place capital at risk; an agreed disaster trigger releases some or all protection to the sponsor.
pays: Sponsor pays risk-transfer costs; investors receive contractual returns.
speed: Calculation and settlement govern receipt; announcement is not proof of receipt.
good: Can provide multi-year external risk capital.
limits: No heat catastrophe bond verified; deal scale and trigger validation may be barriers.
basis: Parametric or modelled-loss trigger may diverge from real loss.

def: A pre-agreed credit line can be drawn when legal and programme conditions are satisfied.
pays: Government repays principal, interest and applicable fees.
speed: Available after drawdown conditions and request; household transfer timing is separate.
good: Pre-arranged liquidity and preparedness incentives.
limits: Debt headroom and declarations can constrain use; heat eligibility is contract-specific.
basis: No insurance basis risk, but a harmful event may not satisfy drawdown conditions.

def: Public spending authority is agreed before a shock so funds can be redirected or released under specified rules.
gets: Authorised departments, suppliers and transfer recipients.
speed: Can be quick only if authority, cash and procurement are ready; no universal observed speed.
good: Can cover common heat needs without insurance attachment.
limits: Other emergencies compete for allocations; no dedicated city heat contingency appropriation verified here.
basis: No insurance index basis risk; allocation and targeting errors remain.

def: Cash or legally earmarked resources are held for eligible disaster spending; dedicated heat funds require explicit rules.
speed: Depends on release rules, liquidity and procurement; no verified heat-specific service standard.
good: Suitable for retained losses and needs that contracts do not cover.
limits: Fund existence does not prove heat eligibility or actual cash availability.
basis: No insurance basis risk; legal and administrative gaps can block relief.

def: A forecast meeting agreed conditions releases pre-arranged resources for specified early actions.
pays: Donors and pooled-fund contributors; not necessarily an insurance premium.
gets: National society, NGOs, suppliers and selected households.
speed: Would ideally fit forecast lead time; action lead time is not verified household cash timing.
good: Can finance public-health action without an insured asset.
limits: Limited geographic coverage and donor replenishment; forecasts can be wrong.
basis: Forecast false positives and missed events; targeting error is distinct.

def: A government pre-agrees forecasts, actions and public release authority for acting before expected heat.
gets: Authorised agencies and people through agreed channels.
speed: Forecast-to-action window would ideally exceed delivery time; not verified for a specific national heat treasury facility.
good: Could institutionalise action beyond project cycles.
limits: National-system design is not established merely because a humanitarian protocol operates nationally.
basis: Forecast error plus administrative and targeting risk.

def: An existing benefit system increases payments or temporarily adds eligible people after a pre-agreed shock.
pays: Public budgets, grants and any linked financing.
speed: Depends on updated registries, enrolment and payment access; drought-system timing is not a heat benchmark.
good: Can extend beyond insured workers to non-working vulnerable people.
limits: Existing exclusions can expand during a shock; employment-linked transfers may require unsafe work.
basis: Index false negatives plus registry and benefit-adequacy errors.

def: A social insurance arrangement compensates eligible work stoppages due to dangerous weather, including heat where explicitly covered.
pays: Employer and worker contributions in the Algerian example.
gets: Eligible workers, potentially through employer payroll.
speed: Payroll and reimbursement deadlines require current administrator verification.
good: Recognises income loss before medical injury.
limits: Contributory employment rules may exclude informal and unregistered workers.
basis: Eligibility and recognition of a work stoppage can miss actual harm.

def: Public or donor money pays part of an insurance premium; design can target affordability while funding transparency and review.
pays: Government or donor; policy buyer may pay the balance.
gets: Insurer receives premium; insured receives only eligible benefits.
speed: Premium is paid at inception/renewal; this is not a disaster payout.
good: Can address affordability and build accessible distribution.
limits: Renewal dependency, weak customer value and poorly targeted subsidies are possible; not findings about a named provider.
basis: Does not remove basis risk; may subsidise a mismatched trigger.

def: A funder pays for verified outputs or outcomes under an agreed contract; financing would ideally bridge the time before verification.
pays: Outcome funder; an investor may bridge costs but is not necessarily the ultimate payer.
speed: Generally after verification; not suitable alone for urgent household liquidity.
good: Can link payment to service performance.
limits: No verified heat-health outcome-payment deal found; energy savings are not proof of lives saved.
basis: Performance-metric mismatch and attribution risk, not weather basis risk.

def: A city commits budget to a specified heat-preparedness service or intervention.
pays: Public budget/donor or sovereign borrower under applicable terms.
gets: Government/city/implementer first; people benefit through separately specified transfers or services.
speed: Operation-specific; institutional settlement and final-recipient receipt would ideally be timed separately.
good: Pre-arrangement can clarify who finances which costs and when.
limits: Legal availability alone does not ensure spending authority or last-mile access.
basis: Administrative and delivery gaps rather than pure index basis risk.

def: Money and actions approved before the season, released when a specified heat forecast crosses its trigger.
pays: Donors or public budget; no individual insurance premium in documented grant models.
gets: Implementing institutions first; people receive defined cash or services.
speed: Protocol-specific; forecast lead, institutional transfer and service/cash receipt are different clocks.
good: Can act on income/health risks before an asset-loss claim exists.
limits: Finite geographic/beneficiary coverage and forecast/delivery constraints.
basis: Missed forecasts, local exposure and targeting exclusions; false alarms possible.

def: Donors pool funds across pre-modelled risks so NGO members can deliver agreed actions on forecast triggers.
pays: Donors or public budget; no individual insurance premium in documented grant models.
gets: Implementing institutions first; people receive defined cash or services.
speed: Protocol-specific; forecast lead, institutional transfer and service/cash receipt are different clocks.
good: Can act on income/health risks before an asset-loss claim exists.
limits: Finite geographic/beneficiary coverage and forecast/delivery constraints.
basis: Missed forecasts, local exposure and targeting exclusions; false alarms possible.

def: UN coordination aligns a forecast trigger, multi-agency actions and pre-arranged finance.
pays: Donors or public budget; no individual insurance premium in documented grant models.
gets: Implementing institutions first; people receive defined cash or services.
speed: Protocol-specific; forecast lead, institutional transfer and service/cash receipt are different clocks.
good: Can act on income/health risks before an asset-loss claim exists.
limits: Finite geographic/beneficiary coverage and forecast/delivery constraints.
basis: Missed forecasts, local exposure and targeting exclusions; false alarms possible.

def: A proposed public appropriation with delegated authority to release money before heat impacts when an approved forecast rule is met.
pays: Donors or public budget; no individual insurance premium in documented grant models.
gets: Implementing institutions first; people receive defined cash or services.
speed: Protocol-specific; forecast lead, institutional transfer and service/cash receipt are different clocks.
good: Can act on income/health risks before an asset-loss claim exists.
limits: Finite geographic/beneficiary coverage and forecast/delivery constraints.
basis: Missed forecasts, local exposure and targeting exclusions; false alarms possible.

n: Public employment with heat-safe working arrangements
def: Government offers eligible people paid work; heat rules can change work conditions. A worksite rule does not itself create a heat cash entitlement.
speed: Payment follows work/muster/payroll rules, not automatically a weather warning.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: Task and attendance rules can conflict with protective rest; full-wage shorter days require explicit authorization.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

def: Existing assistance can pay additional eligible benefits or change when and where people collect; those are different policy choices.
speed: Depends on authorization, registry, liquidity and actual withdrawal; a scheduled launch is not receipt.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: Pre-existing exclusion can persist; a safer payment point alone does not replace lost earnings.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

def: An insured or legally covered worker receives treatment or income support when illness or injury meets benefit rules.
speed: Medical certification and claim review usually precede entitlement; the relevant payroll deadline would ideally be distinguished from observed payment.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: Work attribution, contributions, registration and documentation can exclude heat harm; no standard weather-index basis risk.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

def: Public financing pays for eligible covered care; it is not a grant that a household may spend on anything.
speed: Cashless access/authorization and provider reimbursement are separate clocks.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: It can address medical debt after illness, but not necessarily income loss, outpatient care or preventive rest.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

n: Wage replacement during a heat-related stop
def: A qualifying work interruption activates wage-support rules, allowing covered workers to lose less income while work pauses.
speed: Application, approval and payroll arrangements; observed heat-specific recipient time not verified.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: Employer application and formal employment boundaries matter; worksite exposure can differ from weather-station conditions.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

def: Public support reduces eligible electricity bills or gives a seasonal energy voucher.
speed: Calendar and billing cycle; no automatic forecast trigger unless expressly adopted.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: An account/billing mechanism does not reach everyone without a usable connection or a tenant pass-through arrangement.
basis: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.

def: Pre-agreed assistance uses an existing social registry and delivery channel when an agreed forecast condition is met.
speed: Would ideally arrive before protective actions become impossible; actual transfer time requires transaction evidence.
good: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
limits: Forecast miss/false alarm, stale registers and payment failure remain; a non-heat model requires heat-specific design.
basis: Forecast/impact mismatch plus eligibility and delivery exclusion.

def: An insurer owes a pre-agreed benefit when a named heat index satisfies the contracted rule, rather than valuing every individual's loss.
pays: Members and supporting organisations in the illustrative SEWA cohort; exact premium split not verified.
gets: Covered participants through specified payment arrangements
speed: Case-specific data and claims process; automatic trigger is not immediate usable cash.
good: Can pay without individual loss adjustment.
limits: Needs transparent data/contract and reliable last-mile payment; cannot replace prevention.
basis: Index/exposure, vulnerability, benefit-size, timing and administrative mismatch.

def: Pre-agreed finance and actions activate from a forecast so that assistance can support protective action before the worst impacts.
gets: Implementers first and selected recipients/services through distinct delivery channels
speed: Forecast lead is not recipient delay; readiness, authorization and payment clocks are separate.
good: Can fund action before observed loss.
limits: False alarms, misses, targeting errors and payment delays can remain.
basis: Forecast-impact and targeting mismatch rather than necessarily insurance basis risk.

def: Pays under a contract when a specified heat index crosses a threshold.
speed: No general time-to-money estimate established; separate trigger, insurer settlement and beneficiary receipt.
good: Can avoid individual loss adjustment.
limits: Index mismatch, benefits caps and payment timing remain material.
basis: Weather index can fail to reflect actual harm; grant support also has targeting and coverage gaps.

def: Pre-agreed retained or philanthropic money provides assistance below an insurance threshold.
speed: No general time-to-money estimate established; separate trigger, insurer settlement and beneficiary receipt.
good: Can cover more frequent heat stress.
limits: Funding can expire; it does not transfer risk to an insurer.
basis: Weather index can fail to reflect actual harm; grant support also has targeting and coverage gaps.

def: Grants and advice help governments assemble financing and delivery arrangements.
pays: Development partners; borrowing states for loans
speed: No general time-to-money estimate established; separate trigger, insurer settlement and beneficiary receipt.
good: Can connect funding and social delivery.
limits: Facility existence alone establishes no heat entitlement or beneficiary transfer.
basis: Weather index can fail to reflect actual harm; grant support also has targeting and coverage gaps.
